The four json!({...}) literal input schemas (action.prepare, action.invoke, transaction.begin, handle_input_schema) have NO corresponding entry in 🧬️schema/🦀️.rs's schemas() registry at all — hand-authored, uncatalogued, untraceable to any authoritative module.
inlineSchemas.decision: Move all *_input_schema()/*_output_schema() functions and their json! literals into 🌉️mcp/🧬️schema/🦀️.rs (as schemars-derived structs where a struct exists, or as explicit JSON Schema literals cataloged in schemas()); make 🦀️.rs import named exports instead of calling schemars::schema_for!/json!({...}) directly.
inlineSchemas.openQuestions: Should MCP tool input schemas (which have no corresponding Rust struct — they're loose arg bags) become schemars-derived structs, or should 🧬️schema/🦀️.rs grow a second literal-JSON catalog function alongside schemas()?

alternativeFormats.summary: 426 files across 103 directories, entirely under ✏️s/🔌️plugins/*/🗿️artifacts/*/.../🚪️io/{💡️inferences,📸️snapshot,🔺️diff,🧬️mutations}/{binary,text}/ — a per-plugin, per-io-boundary, per-encoding set of tiny (~100-130 byte) stub/scaffold grammar files (one each of 🅰️.g4, 🔠️.abnf, 🔤️.ebnf, 🥋️.ksy, 🌶️.spicy, 🛰️.proto, 🔗️.graphql, 📖️.grammar.semio, 📡️.protocol.semio), repeated near-identically per plugin. This is a consistent, deliberate structural pattern (not scattered drift), but it lives under a differently-named directory (🚪️io/...) than the goal's 🧬️schema/ convention, and its authoritative-vs-projection status relative to each artifact's own 🧬️schema/ module is undocumented.
alternativeFormats.openQuestion: Is 🚪️io/{inferences,snapshot,diff,mutations}/{binary,text}/ meant to be a second, io-boundary-specific schema-bearing location alongside 🧬️schema/ (analogous to the mcp 🧭️protocol/ question above), or should these files be nested inside/generated from each artifact's 🧬️schema/ module instead?

x-semio-state.meaning: marks a field as ephemeral/runtime state carried in a schema-described payload (seen on UI/session-shaped schemas)

x-semio-derived.meaning: marks a field as computed/derived rather than authored, per schema

x-semio-mutationKinds.meaning: enumerates which mutation kinds a schema/field participates in

x-semio-retained-discriminator.meaning: marks the discriminator field used to distinguish retained/committed variants in a oneOf

x-semio-invariant.meaning: documents an invariant the schema alone cannot express structurally

x-semio-child-kind.meaning: tags the artifact/child kind a schema fragment applies to

x-semio-link-roles.meaning: enumerates valid roles for a link/reference field

x-semio-mutation.meaning: associates a schema fragment with a specific mutation

x-semio-maxEncodedUtf8Bytes.meaning: documents a wire-size budget for an encoded string field

x-semio-maxUtf8Bytes.meaning: documents a raw UTF-8 byte budget for a string field

x-semio-binary.meaning: marks a field/schema as describing binary-encoded payloads

collisions.methodologyNote: Checked all 61722 tracked (git ls-files, minus node_modules/target*/storybook-static/temp/test-results/tickets) paths for: (1) case-insensitive basename/path collisions, (2) Unicode NFC vs NFD normalization producing distinct byte sequences for the 'same' path, (3) presence/absence of the U+FE0F variation selector on emoji path segments. fixtureDirectoryNamingDrift.description: 🧪️fixtures (536 tracked-path occurrences) and 🧫️fixtures (4200 occurrences) are both live, widely-used conventions for the same semantic role across the same products (including sibling instances inside 💻️os), not a rare typo. This directly caused a real duplicate-$id/content-drift bug (see refGraph.duplicateIds: 'https://semio.tech/schemas/os/gis-map-approval-history-fixture-v1.json'): 🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🧪️fixtures/↩️gis-map-approval-history-v1/🧬️.schema.json and 🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🧫️fixtures/↩️gis-map-approval-history-v1/🧬️.schema.json share the identical $id but have DIFFERENT content — one requires 'oldOwnerRetired' with minItems 8/8, the other omits it from 'required' with minItems 9/9.
fixtureDirectoryNamingDrift.action: Needs owner decision: which of 🧪️fixtures/🧫️fixtures is canonical repo-wide, and the stale duplicate under 💻️os needs reconciling (not deleting per this audit's read-only mandate — flagged for the ticket owner)
